cards.front: any vs unknown in one line?
cards.meaning: any means “trust me, don’t check”; unknown means “prove it before you use it.” Both mean the value could be anything; the difference is discipline — same “could be anything,” opposite checking rules.

cards.front: What does any allow that unknown does not?
cards.meaning: any opts out of checking: method calls and property access are allowed, including chains that will fail at runtime. unknown still means “I don’t know”; you must narrow or assert before use.
cards.example: let a: any = 'hello'; a.nonExistentMethod(); a.foo.bar.baz; // compile ok

cards.front: Why is u.toUpperCase() an error when u is unknown?
cards.meaning: unknown forbids operations until you prove the type. After typeof u === 'string', toUpperCase is allowed. Use unknown at boundaries (JSON, catch, untyped APIs); treat any as a last resort.
cards.example: let u: unknown = 'hello'; u.toUpperCase(); // Error — if (typeof u === 'string') u.toUpperCase();

cards.front: Assign to any/unknown vs assign from them?
cards.meaning: Assign to either: almost anything (both are roughly top types). Assign from any to a precise type: allowed without checks — any is also a bottom-ish escape, unsound by design. Assign from unknown to a precise type: error unless narrowed or asserted. Call methods: allowed on any, error on unknown until narrowed.

Anything that touches any often becomes any too — return values, inferred locals — so one any in a helper can disable large regions of the program. Crashes then have no compile signal. unknown would have forced proofs at the use sites.
cards.example: function f(x: any) { return x.foo; } const y = f(1); y.bar; // still any — no error

cards.front: How does any sneak in with noImplicitAny off?
cards.meaning: With noImplicitAny off (or weak inference), untyped parameters become any. function add(a, b) { return a + b } types a and b as any. Enable strict / noImplicitAny; annotate parameters or rely on contextual typing. Turning noImplicitAny off to “save time” infects the function and anything that consumes its returns.
cards.example:
// noImplicitAny: false
function add(a, b) { return a + b; }

cards.front: How do untyped libraries introduce any?
cards.meaning: Modules without types default to any exports (depending on noImplicitAny / skipLibCheck / allowJs). Missing @types/… is a classic infection source. Fix: add types, write a minimal .d.ts, or wrap the API behind a typed facade that takes unknown and validates.

cards.front: What does JSON.parse typically return, and the safe pattern?
cards.meaning: any, historically / typically. Types erase — a User annotation does not validate JSON. Assign to unknown, then validate with a type predicate or Zod. Prefer validate over as User right after parse.
cards.example: const data: unknown = JSON.parse(s); if (isUser(data)) { /* data is User */ }

cards.front: What is catch (err) under useUnknownInCatchVariables, and why not e: any?
cards.meaning: err is unknown. Thrown values can be anything — not only Error. any would allow err.message even when err is a string. unknown forces instanceof Error (or similar) before property access. catch (e: any) is an old habit that opts catch back into contagious any.
cards.example: catch (err) { if (err instanceof Error) console.error(err.message); else console.error(String(err)); }

cards.meaning: as any and // @ts-ignore to silence errors. Other leaks: Object.keys / some DOM APIs returning wide types (less extreme than any, but similar “widen then cast” habits), and loosely typed test mocks.

cards.front: Why is T = any a leak?
cards.meaning: A generic default written as T = any reintroduces contagious any whenever callers omit the type argument. Prefer T = unknown (as in Page<T = unknown>) when a default is needed.

At boundaries: JSON, catch, external APIs, message ports. Boundary in: unknown → narrow/validate → typed domain. Boundary out: serialize known types; don’t trust round-trips without parsing. You can pass unknown around as a passthrough (logValue(v: unknown)); you cannot operate on it as structured data without checks.

cards.front: When do people still use any, honestly?
cards.meaning: Rare, conscious cases: migrating a huge JS file (temporary); truly unrepresentable interop (wrap and shrink the blast radius); exhausted type-system edge cases (document why; prefer unknown + assert). Never as the default for “I’ll fix types later” in new Nest/React code. Prefer: 1) unknown + narrowing, 2) generics, 3) proper typings, 4) any only with a comment and a ticket to remove it.

cards.front: const user = u as User after JSON.parse — safer than any?
cards.meaning: It compiles with no runtime proof. Assertions are sometimes needed, but they are not safer than any if you assert wrongly. Prefer predicates or Zod, then assertion only at a validated boundary.

cards.front: Object or {} vs unknown for unvalidated input?
cards.meaning: Prefer unknown for “yet unvalidated.” Object and {} have different assignability quirks and do not force the same narrowing discipline.
